st01.run:
Extreme wide from high up in the top tier of a British football stadium at night, looking down across the whole bowl to a temporary stage built at the far end of the pitch. Every LED floodlight bank on the roof rim is on full, cool daylight-white, throwing hard flat light down onto the stands and the grass. Thin haze hangs over the pitch so the beams from the stage rig show as pale shafts, magenta and amber, crossing the white of the floods. The man from the reference stands small and far off on the stage behind a DJ table, both arms thrown up, the only figure on it. The pitch and every stand are packed solid with adults, a mixed crowd of all ages and backgrounds in hoodies, football shirts, puffer jackets, work hi-vis and going-out clothes, thousands of arms up at once, people standing on seats, a flare of spilled beer catching the light in the near rows. The near tier is in the bottom of the frame, slightly soft, backs of heads and raised arms; the far side of the bowl recedes into haze. Advertising boards round the pitch are plain dark panels. Long lens compression, slightly off-centre, horizon a touch tilted, as if a camera operator on the gantry grabbed it. Shot on an ARRI Alexa 35, 16:9.
Thanks.

st01d.run:
Keep the exact framing, camera position, stadium and crowd layout of the first reference image. Change only the light: every floodlight bank is off and every stage beam is off. The stadium is almost pitch black. The only light source is the small green-lit screen of the man from the second reference, far off on the stage, a tiny green point in a huge black bowl, throwing a faint green wash on the DJ table and the few metres of stage around him. The stands and pitch are black shapes; only the nearest row of heads at the bottom of the frame is just readable as dark outlines against the faint haze. The roof rim and the dead floodlight banks are barely visible as darker lines against a dull orange city sky at the very top of the frame. Deep underexposure, heavy shadow grain, as shot at high ISO on an ARRI Alexa 35.
Thanks.

st02.run:
Close-up of the head of the man from the reference, framed from the top of the shoulders up, seen from slightly below and a little off to the side so the curve of the tube and the casing edge show. His screen has just come on hard: the word "BADCODE" in blocky green capitals fills the glass, straight and front-on, sharp and readable, with the faint horizontal scan lines of an old tube visible across the letters. The green light from the screen is the only light in the frame and falls on his shoulders and the cables hanging behind him; below the shoulders his body drops into black. Behind him the stadium is a total black void with faint haze picking up a little of the green. Shot on a Sony FX3 at high ISO, shadow grain, the screen slightly overexposed at the brightest letter edges.
Thanks.

st03.run:
Low angle from the top row of a stadium stand, looking steeply up at one LED floodlight bank on the roof edge against a black night sky: a big steel frame holding rows of square lamp heads, about a dozen across and four rows deep. The bottom two rows are on, hard cool white, the rest are still dark grey glass. The light from the lit rows rakes down through thin haze in straight beams and catches the steel girders, cable runs and a gantry walkway. A dark roof edge cuts across the bottom corner of the frame. Shot on an ARRI Alexa 35, wide lens, the lit lamps clipping to white, the dark lamps showing their metal reflectors.
Thanks.

st04.run:
Mid-wide from the floor of the pitch, about twenty metres back from the stage, at head height in the crowd. The man from the reference stands centre-left behind a long DJ table on a high stage, both arms flung straight up, his screen lit green. Behind and above him the stage rig is lit: white and amber beams fanning out through haze, the stadium floodlights blazing white across the stand behind the stage, the top tier packed with people. In the foreground, in the bottom third of the frame, the backs of heads and raised arms of the crowd, hard-lit from the stage, slightly soft with a long lens: a shaved head, a woman's braids, a bucket hat, a raised pint, a phone held up. Long lens compression so the stage looks huge behind him. Shot on an ARRI Alexa 35, a little off-centre, the beams clipping to white.
Thanks.

st04d.run:
Keep the exact framing, camera position, stage, the man's pose and the foreground crowd of the first reference image. Change only the light: the stadium floodlights and all the stage beams are off. One single narrow white spotlight from high behind the stage points straight down onto the man from the second reference, catching the top of his casing and his raised arms in a hard rim, his screen a dim green. Everything else is black. The foreground heads and raised arms are pure black silhouettes against that one pool of light and the haze around it. The stand behind the stage is invisible. Heavy underexposure, shadow grain, shot on an ARRI Alexa 35 at high ISO.
Thanks.

st05.run:
Medium close from the stage side of the front barrier, looking down slightly into the front rows of a stadium crowd, lit hard and white from the stage above and behind the camera, with a magenta beam cutting across the back rows. Adults pressed against the steel barrier, mid-scream, mouths open, arms straight up: a big bald man in his fifties in a football shirt with sweat on his scalp, a young Black woman in a puffer jacket with her braids flying, a South Asian lad in a tracksuit top with his fist up, a white woman in her forties in a denim jacket bellowing, an older Caribbean man in a flat cap with both hands raised, a young East Asian woman on someone's shoulders behind. Hands grip the barrier, a pint cup tips and spills over it. The rows behind go soft quickly with a long lens into raised arms and phone lights. Off-centre, slightly tilted. Shot on a Sony FX3, shadows deep, highlights on skin clipping a little.
Thanks.

st06.run:
Medium shot up in a steep upper stand of a football stadium, shot from a few rows lower and to the side, looking up into a dense knot of fans standing on their seats. The stand is floodlit cool white from the roof, flat and hard. A mixed group of adults all ages and backgrounds bouncing together, arms round each other's shoulders: a ginger man in a Harrington jacket, a Black woman in a hi-vis work vest straight from a shift, two older men in anoraks, a Turkish lad in a bucket hat, a woman with a shaved head in a band T-shirt. Football scarves held stretched overhead, one swung round in a circle. Plastic pint cups thrown up, beer spraying in arcs against the white light. Dark seat rows and a concrete stairway run up behind them to the roof edge. Long lens, the people further up going soft. Shot on an ARRI Alexa 35, slightly tilted, off-centre.
Thanks.

st07.run:
From behind and slightly to one side of the man from the reference, standing at the front edge of the stage, seen from about waist height so his shoulders and the back of his casing fill the left third of the frame, cables hanging down his back. His screen faces away from camera; its green light spills on the edges of his casing and his shoulders. Beyond him the whole stadium is lit: every floodlight bank on the roof blazing cool white, the pitch and every tier packed with a crowd, arms up as far as the eye goes, beams from the stage behind the camera sweeping out over them through haze. The crowd is soft with distance, a field of raised arms and bodies. He is dark against it, a black shape rimmed by the light. Shot on an ARRI Alexa 35, slightly tilted, the far floodlights clipping to white.
Thanks.

du01.run:
A supermarket car park at night in steady rain, 16:9. Two men face each other in the middle of a painted parking bay, a hand's width apart. Man A, from the first reference image (rough-duct-tape.jpg), stands on the left of frame. Man B, from the second reference image (posh-tweed.jpg), stands on the right. Man A is hunched forward from the waist, head jutted toward Man B's face, rapping into it. His right hand grips a brown beer bottle by the neck and is caught mid-jab toward Man B's chest, the bottle's base an inch from his lapel. Man B leans back from the hips, chin pulled in, shoulders raised, his right hand holding a champagne flute half full of champagne down by his hip, close to his body. Camera at chest height, 35mm, a tight side-on two-shot so both heads sit on the same line. Behind them: wet black tarmac with white bay lines, two small dome tents pitched in the bays, a steel oil drum burning low with orange fire, and further back the green-lit front of a supermarket with its shutters down. The fire throws hard orange light on the side of both men nearest it; the rest is cold sodium-lamp yellow and wet shadow. Rain streaks visible in the firelight, puddles broken by drops. No lettering anywhere.
Thanks.

du02.run:
Night, the same supermarket car park in rain, 16:9. Over-the-shoulder shot: Man A, from the first reference image (rough-duct-tape.jpg), is in the left foreground, seen from behind his right shoulder, out of focus, his shoulder and the back of his head filling the left third of the frame. Man B, from the second reference image (posh-tweed.jpg), faces the camera in the right two-thirds, sharp, a step from Man A. Man B has come forward now: chest pushed out, shoulders square, head tilted down at Man A, rapping hard. His right arm is extended with the champagne flute held by the stem, the rim pointed straight at Man A like a finger. Camera at Man A's shoulder height, 50mm. Behind Man B: a row of empty painted bays, a shopping trolley on its side, a tent with a tarp weighted by bricks, and the green front of the supermarket out of focus. Lit from the left by the orange barrel fire just off frame, cool yellow lamp light from above, rain falling in front of the lamps. Wet tarmac reflecting the fire as broken orange streaks. No lettering anywhere.
Thanks.

du03.run:
Night, supermarket car park in rain, 16:9. Man A, from the first reference image (rough-duct-tape.jpg), on the left, and Man B, from the second reference image (posh-tweed.jpg), on the right, stand shoulder to shoulder, both squared up to the camera, both rapping straight into the lens at the same moment. Both are hunched slightly forward, knees bent, weight low. Man A's beer bottle is held at chest height in his left hand, his right hand cutting down in front of him. Man B's champagne flute is in his right hand at chest height, his left hand cutting down in the same gesture as Man A's, mirrored. Low camera at waist height, 28mm, looking up a little, both men filling the frame from mid-thigh up. Behind them in the gap between their heads: the burning oil drum and, beyond it, the green supermarket front and a lamp post with rain falling through its light. Tents in the bays to either side. Hard orange firelight from behind them rims their shoulders; their fronts lit by cold lamp light. No lettering anywhere.
Thanks.

du04.run:
Night, supermarket car park in rain, 16:9. Medium shot of the man from the reference image (posh-tweed.jpg) alone, standing in a parking bay, frame centre-right. He is rapping with a sneer in his posture: chin raised, shoulders back, one hip cocked. His right arm swings out wide holding a champagne flute by the stem, the glass pointed out at the car park around him as if presenting it. His left hand is open at his side, palm up. Behind him and to the left, filling the frame: a row of bays with three tents, a camping chair with a carrier bag on it, a burning oil drum, a trolley full of blankets, and the green front of the supermarket, its car park lamps lighting the rain. Camera at eye height, 35mm, off to his right so he faces across frame toward the left edge. Orange firelight on his left side, cold lamp light from above. Wet tarmac shining. No lettering anywhere.
Thanks.

du05.run:
Night, supermarket car park in rain, 16:9. Medium close-up of the man from the reference image (rough-duct-tape.jpg) alone, frame left, facing toward frame right where the other man's shoulder is just visible as an out-of-focus dark shape at the right edge. He is rapping fierce and bitter: hunched over, head thrust forward, shoulders up near his ears. His right hand is up close to his face, two fingers pointed hard at the man off-frame; his left hand clenches the neck of a beer bottle against his own chest. Camera at his eye height, 50mm, tight. Behind him, out of focus: the barrel fire, a tent, the green supermarket front, rain streaking through lamp light. Hard orange firelight across the side of his head and hand, cold blue-yellow shadow on the other side. Raindrops sitting on his shoulders. No lettering anywhere.
Thanks.

du06.run:
Night, supermarket car park in rain, 16:9. Medium shot of the man from the reference image (posh-tweed.jpg) alone, standing at the edge of a parking bay beside a tent, frame centre. The fight has gone out of him: shoulders dropped and rounded, head bowed so he looks at the wet tarmac a metre in front of him, his body turned a little away from frame left where the other man stands off-screen. His right arm hangs by his side, the champagne flute dangling from two fingers by the stem, tipped, nearly empty, a drip falling from the rim. His left hand is loose at his thigh. Camera slightly above eye height, 50mm, looking down at him a touch. Behind him the supermarket front is out of focus, the barrel fire low and further away now, lamp light catching the rain. Less firelight on him than before; mostly cold lamp light from above, his shadow pooled at his feet. No lettering anywhere.
Thanks.

du07.run:
Night, supermarket car park in rain, 16:9. Medium close-up of the man from the reference image (rough-duct-tape.jpg) alone, frame left, facing toward frame right where the other man is off-screen. His anger has drained: shoulders lowered, back straightened from the hunch, head tilted slightly to one side. His left hand is flat on his own chest over his heart. His right hand holds the beer bottle low at his hip, loosely. Camera at eye height, 50mm. Behind him, out of focus: the burning oil drum, two tents, the green supermarket front. Warm orange firelight on his front from the barrel, softer than before, rain falling through it. No lettering anywhere.
Thanks.

du08.run:
Night, supermarket car park in rain, 16:9. Extreme close-up insert, hands and drinks only, no faces in frame. From frame left, the right hand of the man in the first reference image (rough-duct-tape.jpg) holds a brown glass beer bottle around its body, thumb on one side, four fingers wrapped round the other. From frame right, the right hand of the man in the second reference image (posh-tweed.jpg) holds a champagne flute by its stem between thumb and two fingers, the bowl of the flute tilted toward the bottle. The rim of the flute and the shoulder of the bottle are two centimetres apart, about to touch, in the centre of the frame. Raindrops on the glass of both, beads running down the bottle. Behind, deep out of focus: orange fire from the burning drum and a band of green from the supermarket front. Hard orange firelight catching the edges of the glass. Camera at the height of the drinks, 85mm, tight. No lettering anywhere, the bottle has no readable label.

du09.run:
Night, supermarket car park in rain, 16:9. Man A, from the first reference image (rough-duct-tape.jpg), on the left, and Man B, from the second reference image (posh-tweed.jpg), on the right, stand side by side at the same height, facing straight into the camera. Man A's left arm is round Man B's shoulders, his hand gripping Man B's far shoulder; Man B's right arm is round Man A's shoulders, his hand on Man A's far shoulder. Man A's free right hand raises the beer bottle high above his head; Man B's free left hand raises the champagne flute high above his. Both are mid-shout at the lens, heads thrown slightly back, chests out. Low camera at waist height, 24mm, close, so their raised drinks reach the top of the frame. Behind them the burning oil drum sends sparks up, tents in the bays either side, the green supermarket front and a lamp post with heavy rain falling through its light. Orange firelight from behind rims both men; cold lamp light on their fronts. No lettering anywhere.
Thanks.

re01.run:
Use the two men from the attached image: the man on the left in the image is Bob, the man on the right is Tarquin. Wide shot, camera at chest height at the far end of a supermarket car park at night, in rain. Wet black tarmac with worn white bay lines running away from camera, puddles holding broken reflections of the sodium lamps. Along the back, the supermarket front with its green fascia and shutters half down. Three small dome tents pitched inside the painted bays, a shopping trolley on its side, cardboard flattened under one tent. Frame right, middle distance: Bob stands beside a rusted oil drum with fire inside it, side-on to camera, his head turned sharply towards the left of frame, one hand still held out over the heat. Frame left, nearer the entrance ramp: Tarquin walking into the car park towards him, shoulders hunched against the rain, hands in his pockets, wet through, small in the open space of empty bays. The two men are about fifteen metres apart with nothing between them but wet tarmac. Firelight on Bob's side of the frame, flat orange lamp light on Tarquin's side. Rain visible as streaks against the dark. 16:9.
Thanks.

re02.run:
Use the two men from the attached image: Bob is the man on the left in the image, Tarquin the man on the right. Medium two-shot from the side, camera at eye level, both men in profile facing each other about an arm's length apart, Bob on the left of frame, Tarquin on the right. Bob has stepped in: chest forward, chin pushed out, right arm extended with the index finger jabbing at Tarquin's face, mouth wide open mid-shout, brow pulled down hard. Tarquin leans back from the waist, head turned slightly away, eyes on the finger, hands half raised at his chest. Behind them, out of focus, a dome tent in a painted bay and the green supermarket front. The oil drum fire sits just out of frame left, throwing orange light across Bob's side and onto the side of Tarquin's face. Rain falling between them, both men soaked, water running off their hands. Night. 16:9.
Thanks.

re03.run:
Use the two men from the attached image: Bob is the man on the left in the image, Tarquin the man on the right. Over-the-shoulder shot from behind Bob's left shoulder, which fills the left third of the frame dark and out of focus. Tarquin takes the other two thirds, facing camera, shouting back: mouth open, teeth showing, neck tight, eyes narrowed at Bob. His right arm is flung out wide to the side, open hand pointing back at the row of small tents in the painted bays and the green-lit supermarket front behind him, as if to say look at all this. His left hand clenched at his side. Wet hair stuck to his forehead, rain hitting his shoulders. The burning drum off frame throws warm light up one side of his face; the background is the wet car park, tents, a trolley, the shop sign, rain streaks against the dark. Night. 16:9.
Thanks.

re04.run:
Use Tarquin, the man on the right in the attached image. Close-up on Tarquin, framed from the collarbones up, slightly off-centre to the right, camera just below his eye line. He is mid-breath after shouting: mouth only just open, jaw loosening, brow still creased but the eyes starting to drop. Rain running down his forehead and dripping off his nose and chin. Firelight from the left of frame warms one cheek; the other side is in cold orange lamp light and shadow. Behind him, far out of focus, the green supermarket sign and the soft shapes of tents. Night, rain. 16:9.

re05.run:
Use Bob, the man on the left in the attached image. Close-up on Bob, from the collarbones up, slightly off-centre to the left, camera at his eye line. He is still hard-faced from shouting: jaw set, nostrils flared, eyes fixed on someone just off frame right. Rain on his face and shoulders, water dripping from his eyebrows. The fire in the drum is close beside him off frame left, throwing strong orange light across his face from the side and moving shadows on his cheek. Behind him, out of focus, wet tarmac, a painted bay line and the dark shape of a tent. Night. 16:9.

re06.run:
Use the two men from the attached image: Bob is the man on the left in the image, Tarquin the man on the right. Medium two-shot from the side at waist height, the rusted oil drum with fire inside it between them in the lower centre of frame, Bob on the left, Tarquin on the right, both at the same height, side-on to camera. Bob holds his right arm out across the top of the barrel, offering a dented silver beer can, his fingers wrapped round the middle of it. Tarquin reaches for it, head still a little lowered, his right hand open, fingers just touching the bottom half of the can below Bob's hand. Both soaked. Firelight from below lights both their faces and the can. Behind them, out of focus, tents in the painted bays and the green supermarket front in the rain. Night. 16:9.

ly01.run: Use only the man on the right of the reference image; leave the man on the left out of the picture entirely. He stands alone at night in an open supermarket car park in steady rain, half turned from the camera, head tipped back, a cheap clear plastic bottle of spirits upended at his mouth, his free hand hanging at his side. Behind him, out of focus: wet black tarmac with painted white bay lines, two small tents pitched in the bays, and a burning oil drum throwing orange light low across the puddles. The only other light is the cold green of a supermarket front far behind him and one sodium lamp on a pole. Rain streaks visible against the lamp. Waist-up, shot from a little below on a 50mm lens, handheld, slightly off-centre, his face partly in shadow. Shot on Kodak Vision3 500T, the night left properly dark. 16:9. Thanks.

ly02.run: Use only the man on the right of the reference image; leave the man on the left out of the picture entirely. Daytime on the bare concrete floor of a warehouse loading bay. He lies on his side on the dusty concrete, knees drawn up, one hand pressed flat into the small of his back, the other palm down on the floor, his face screwed tight with pain, teeth clenched, eyes shut. A split sack of cement lies beside him where he dropped it, grey powder spilled across the floor in a fan, and a steel sack trolley stands tipped over just behind. Flat grey daylight comes in from an open roller door on the left; the far end of the bay is in shadow with stacked pallets. Low camera, almost at floor level, about two metres away, 35mm lens, his body across the frame on a slight diagonal. Dust hangs in the daylight. Shot on Kodak Vision3 250D. 16:9. Thanks.

ly03.run: A trading floor at night with nobody at it. A long row of desks, each with four or six monitors on arms, every chair empty and turned at a different angle, a jacket left over one chair back, a half-drunk coffee in a paper cup. The monitors show blurred scrolling columns of red and green figures and jagged line charts, too fast and too soft to read, the only light in the room, throwing coloured light up onto the empty desks and keyboards. Ceiling lights off; the floor-to-ceiling windows at the back show dark office towers with a few lit windows. Shot from the end of the row at desk height, 35mm lens, the row of screens receding to the right. Shot on Kodak Vision3 500T, the room dark apart from the screens. No readable lettering anywhere. 16:9. Thanks.

ly04.run: A car park exit barrier at night in heavy rain, seen close from the driver's side. The red and white striped barrier arm lies down across the exit lane, beaded with rain, water dripping off its tip. The squat grey barrier post beside it has one small round lamp lit solid red, its red light catching the raindrops on the arm and a red smear on the wet tarmac below. Beyond the arm the exit road is empty and dark, one sodium street lamp far off. The edge of a car bonnet sits wet and out of focus in the bottom of the frame. Camera at the height of a driver's window, 50mm lens, the arm crossing the frame from left to right. Shot on Kodak Vision3 500T, the night left dark. No readable lettering anywhere. 16:9. Thanks.

ly05.run: A glass-walled boardroom on the top floor of a City tower at dusk, empty. A long dark wood table runs away from the camera, a row of black leather chairs pushed back from it at careless angles as if everyone left at once, one chair turned to the window. On the table: a closed laptop, a water jug, a few glasses with water still in them, a pen. A large wall screen at the far end and two smaller screens on the table show slow-moving blurred charts and a video-call grid of empty dark tiles, no readable text. Through the glass, the river and the city lights below in the blue last light of the day. Ceiling lights off; the room lit by the dusk outside and the screens. Shot from the near end of the table at seated height, 28mm lens, slightly off the centre line. Shot on Kodak Vision3 250D. 16:9. Thanks.

ly06.run: Inside a large distribution warehouse at night, the main lights off. A long aisle of tall steel racking stretches away from the camera; low squat orange robots carry shelving pods along the floor, each with one small blue status lamp, and a robotic picking arm works at a station halfway down, lit by its own white work light. In the foreground on the right, by a steel fire door, a row of hooks on a breeze-block wall holds six empty hi-vis vests in yellow and orange hanging limp, one fallen on the floor beneath, a pair of worn work boots under the hooks. Cold light from the arm's work station and the blue lamps; deep shadow everywhere else. Camera at chest height beside the hooks, 35mm lens, the vests sharp in the foreground and the aisle soft behind. Shot on Kodak Vision3 500T. No readable lettering anywhere. 16:9. Thanks.

ly07.run: Close on a city gutter at night in hammering rain. One sodden banknote lies flat in the running water against the kerb, half pressed into a drain grate, its edge torn and curling, its print soft and too blurred to read. Rainwater sheets over it and drops burst around it. A cigarette end and a crushed can sit beside it. Light comes from a sodium street lamp out of frame, orange on the wet stone kerb and the water, with one cold white reflection from a shop window across the road. Camera very low, a few centimetres off the road surface, 85mm lens, the banknote sharp and the street behind it dissolved into soft dark shapes. Shot on Kodak Vision3 500T, the night kept dark. No readable lettering anywhere. 16:9. Thanks.

st11d.run:
Night, inside a huge British football stadium, 16:9. Every floodlight bank on the roof rim is off and every stage light is off. The camera stands on the pitch in the middle of the crowd, about thirty metres back from a temporary stage at the far end, at head height, 35mm, locked off and level. The man from the reference stands centre stage behind a DJ table, facing straight out at the crowd and the camera, his whole body square to us, both hands on the decks. He is big enough in the frame to read clearly: he fills about a quarter of the frame's height. His screen shows the word BADCODE, steady and sharp, and it is the main light on the stage: a hard green light falling on the DJ table, his hands, his chest and a few metres of stage boards around him, then dropping off into black. Between the camera and the stage the crowd is a dense field of dark heads and shoulders in silhouette against that green, a few arms raised as black shapes. Behind and above him the stands rise as a vast black bowl, only the curve of the roof rim and the dead floodlight banks visible as darker lines against a dull orange city sky. Thin haze hangs low over the crowd. Every big screen and advertising board in the stadium is off and black. Deep shadows, heavy grain, as shot at high ISO on an ARRI Alexa 35. Ominous, still, waiting.
Thanks.

st11p.run:
The exact same frame as the reference image: the same camera position, lens and framing, the same stage, the same man behind the DJ table in the same pose facing the camera with BADCODE on his screen, the same crowd in the same places. Change only the light: at this instant every floodlight bank on the roof rim fires at once, a hard flat white light slamming down over the whole bowl. The stands are suddenly visible, packed to the roof with adults, the crowd on the pitch lit from above in hard white with sharp black shadows under every head and arm, the haze lit white over the pitch. The stage and the man are lit flat white from above too, his screen still showing BADCODE in green. The sky above the roof goes black against the light. Hard, harsh, cold, like a power surge: no lens flare, crisp edges, the floodlight banks reading as rows of flat white panels. Same grain, as shot on an ARRI Alexa 35, 16:9.
Thanks.

du06x.run:
Night, supermarket car park in rain, 16:9. Medium shot of the man from the reference image (posh-tweed.jpg) alone, standing at the edge of a parking bay beside a tent, frame centre.
